title: Exemplar evaporation — debug lab and testbed
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad to catalog investigations into what I’m calling 'exemplar evaporation' — the observed weakening or shifting of few-shot exemplar influence in generation as context, tokenization, or model state changes. This is a working note: lots of half-baked ideas, small experiments, and reproducible test cases.

Background / hypothesis:
- Observed in multiple runs: identical few-shot exemplars have different utility depending on prefix length, token boundaries around examples, and whether preceding system instructions are present.
- Hypothesis A: exemplar tokens get 'diluted' by KV-cache eviction/precision in long contexts on certain quantized kernels.
- Hypothesis B: exemplar semantics shift because the model reweights recency signals when prompts include variable meta-data (timestamps, user ids).
- Hypothesis C: tokenization artifacts (leading/trailing spaces, Unicode punctuation) change pattern matching for mimicry.

High-level goals:
1) Produce a small, deterministic test harness (2–3 prompts, 5 seeds each) to reproduce evaporation in both hosted and private deployments.
2) Create compact exemplar variants (canonical vs. token-split vs. soft-masked) to measure influence.
3) Surface short-term mitigations: engineered priming, sentinel tokens, or deliberate example redundancy.

Quick experiment matrix (mini):
- Models: rwd-13b-v1 (float16), open-7b-q4, rwd-3b-8bit
- Context modes: (A) short system + 2 exemplars, (B) long system + 2 exemplars, (C) short system + 2 exemplars + unrelated noisy paragraph before query
- Exemplars: canonical (clean text), split-token (insert zero-width spaces at boundaries), sentinel-wrapped (<<EX1>>...<<END>>), redundant (repeat each exemplar twice)
- Metrics: exemplar imitation rate (string n-gram overlap with exemplar answer), instruction-following score (manual rubric), top-1 token divergence after exemplar boundary (small heuristic)

Repro test (seedable):
(Format for runs)
-- PROMPT TEMPLATE --
System: You are a concise assistant.
Exemplar 1: Q: Convert the sentence to passive voice. A: "The committee approved the plan." -> "The plan was approved by the committee."
Exemplar 2: Q: Convert to passive. A: "Someone will fix the bug." -> "The bug will be fixed by someone."
Query: Q: Convert to passive. A:
-- END TEMPLATE --
Run variants: add a 200-token irrelevant paragraph before Query; insert an emoji between exemplars; surround exemplars with <<E>> tags.

Preliminary notes / observations (runs 2025-01-20 to 2025-01-24):
- On rwd-13b-v1, baseline short-system case produced exact exemplar style 78% of runs. Adding a noisy paragraph dropped imitation to ~42%.
- On open-7b-q4 the drop was steeper (81% -> 33%) and hallucination-like paraphrases increased.
- Token-split exemplar (zero-width space) sometimes improved recall on smaller models but made output brittle on streaming mode.
- Repeating exemplars (redundant) helps but increases token cost; diminishing returns after 2 repeats.

Failure cases catalog (short):
- Case: exemplar answer uses colloquial phrasing. Evaporation leads to more formal paraphrase even when exemplar is informal.
- Case: exemplars with punctuation-heavy answers influence punctuation reproduction unpredictably (comma placement lost).
- Case: exemplar uses rare named entity: model will sometimes invent alternate entity with similar suffix rather than copying exactly.

Probes to add (to make this more reproducible):
- Token-level alignment: log token ids around exemplar boundaries, run with identical seed and record first-100 KV-cache states where possible (private deployment only).
- Truncation stress: gradually increase preceding system/meta content in 100-token steps and measure imitation slope.
- Soft-masking test: replace content words in exemplars with placeholders and measure if structure-only copies survive.

Short-term mitigations to try in prod (low-effort):
- Sentinels + explicit 'copy style from the examples exactly' instruction right before the Query.
- Local exemplar repetition with small paraphrase variations (robust ensemble).
- Use a short context window that places exemplars immediately adjacent to query (if routing/policy allows).

For instrumentation/ops:
- Add a per-request debug flag that returns the top-8 logits for tokens immediately after the last exemplar. Use only in private or debug tenants.
- Add metric: exemplar-copy-rate per model per route, surfaced in console as a percent over rolling 24h.

Notes-to-self:
- Share small CSV of runs (seed, model, config, imitation-score) with Lina and Ethan.
- Open a tiny Linear ticket to track 'exemplar-evaporation reproducible harness' (attach scripts and seeds).
- Try same experiments with longer, diverse exemplars (not just passive-voice) to see if effect generalizes beyond syntactic transformations.

Example odd-bug transcript (raw):
Prompt variant: repeated exemplars + emoji between them
Model output: "The plan was approved by the committee" -> succeeded
Next run identical seed: "The plan had been approved by that committee" -> paraphrase introduced; exemplar phrase expected unchanged
My notes: need to capture logits and top-k at boundary to see whether model started diverging before query token or at generation time.

Unresolved questions (brain-dump):
- Are we seeing true 'evaporation' (loss of exemplar signal) or is the model opportunistically optimizing for generality when context length increases?
- How much is quantization/kernerl precision vs. prompt formatting?
- Can we derive a cheap heuristic for routing to stronger models when exemplar-copy-rate drops below threshold?

Actionable next steps (this week):
- Finalize reproducible template and commit harness to github (1 day).
- Run broad matrix over 3 models and capture outputs + imitation metric (2 days).
- Sync with Lina to add debug flag for per-request logits on private infra (blocker: infra approval).

Random micro-ideas (might revisit):
- Use directional embedding anchoring: compute exemplar embedding and bias decoding towards tokens that increase embedding similarity in KV-space. Risky but fun.
- Small 'style fingerprint' classifier to estimate whether output matches exemplar style; surface as eval metric.

End notes:
This doc is intentionally messy. Keep it here as a living scratchpad until we have a reproducible artifact to promote to product/obs ticket.

-- Maya 2025-02-02
